# ShopPal v2: Full documentation

> ShopPal v2 is an AI shopping agent for the PayPal AI Hackathon. It acts for the buyer, not the seller: it scores sellers, shows the honest PayPal total before payment, predicts hold risk, and auto-saves proof for disputes. The demo runs on PayPal Sandbox, no real money moves.

## Demos

- Static demo (GitHub Pages + PayPal JS SDK): https://fhria5.github.io/shoppal-v2/
- Live-server demo (Cloudflare Worker API): https://fhria5.github.io/shoppal-v2/live/
- Source code (GitHub): https://github.com/fhria5/shoppal-v2

## The problem

PayPal users face held funds, layered fees that can reach roughly 10% on a $50 cross-border purchase, disputes lost despite having proof, risky sellers they cannot vet, and subscriptions that keep charging unnoticed. These are the top complaints in PayPal user reviews, and no shopping tool shows the buyer the full picture before they pay.

## How it works

Type what you want in plain language ("headphones under $60") and ShopPal:

1. Finds matching products, ranked safest first, with a Seller Risk Score.
2. Shows the honest total before checkout, including every PayPal fee.
3. Predicts hold risk, so buyers know whether their money may be frozen.
4. Checks out through PayPal Sandbox (Orders API v2, verified capture).
5. Auto-saves proof to a Proof Vault and drafts a factual dispute response from that proof.

## Features in detail

### AI Seller Risk Score (0–100)

Built from four transparent components: profile age (25 points), transaction history (35), price fairness (20), and tracking/returns (20). Zones: 80–100 Safe, 50–79 Caution, 0–49 Risky. Scores are auditable rules; the AI (Vyce / DeepSeek) only rewrites the reasons in plain language and never changes a number.

### Honest Total Cost

Item price plus PayPal Checkout fee (3.49% + $0.49), international fee (1.5%), and currency conversion spread (~3.5%). Example: a $59.99 item costs $65.57 in total. The demo also shows the cost of things going wrong: chargeback $20, dispute $15 ($30 high-volume), refund keeps the original fee, instant transfer 1.5%, and the cheaper Micropayments rate for items under $12, plus whether the purchase is covered by PayPal Buyer Protection (Goods & Services, not Friends & Family).

### Hold Predictor and Hold Release Checklist

The Hold Predictor estimates the chance a seller's PayPal funds will be held (Low / Moderate / High) from public hold patterns. The Hold Release Checklist shows the steps that release a hold early, from PayPal's published rules: add a tracking number (release 3 days after delivery), mark the order as Shipped (7 days after the ship date), ask the buyer to confirm receipt (1 day after confirmation), or wait 21 days by default. Steps are pre-ticked from the seller's own data where known; the rest are interactive checkboxes that recompute the estimated release live.

### Proof Vault

Every completed Sandbox checkout is saved with the verified capture, risk score, and total. After purchase, the vault lets you check the live order status (Orders + Payments API re-verification) and refund a capture in one tap (Payments API v2, full or partial). Re-capturing an already-captured order recovers the existing capture instead of erroring.

### Dispute Win Simulator and Evidence Pack

Before you buy, the simulator tells you the chance of winning a PayPal dispute if the purchase goes wrong (rule-based, with the missing proof listed so you can collect it first). After purchase, it simulates from the saved proof. The Evidence Pack downloads a printable proof page (order, verified capture, risk score, timeline) ready to attach to a PayPal dispute.

### PayPal Phishing Check

Paste any message claiming to be from PayPal and get a verdict (0–100) from rule-based signals, lookalike-domain detection (paypa1, pay-pal), urgency language, requests for passwords or OTP codes, generic greetings, link/text mismatch, plus an AI review from Vyce.

### Import Cost

Duty + VAT/GST per destination country, shown in the honest-total bubble. Indonesia: 7.5% duty + 11% VAT (verified against PMK 96/2023 + PMK 4/2025; FOB under US$3 is duty-free but VAT still applies). United States: $0 under the $800 de minimis. EU: 19% VAT. UK: 20% VAT. Singapore: 9% GST. The same $60 headphones cost $71.60 in Indonesia and $60 in the US. Always labelled an estimate, exact duty depends on the product HS code.

### Compare 2 Products

Pick any two products and see risk, honest total, hold, seller, and tracking/returns side by side. On phones the table scrolls horizontally inside the chat bubble instead of overflowing the screen.

### Monthly Budget

Set a monthly budget (stored in the browser). The Proof Vault shows this month's spend against it, and the checkout warns before a purchase would push you over.

### Check Any Link and Deadline Tracker

Paste any product URL and ShopPal reads the page's public metadata (title, price, image) and scores the domain and the price against the demo catalog median. The Deadline Tracker counts down the 180-day dispute-filing deadline, the 20-day escalation deadline, and the seller's 30-day return window from every purchase in the vault.

## API

The server exposes a REST API (same routes on the Express server and the Cloudflare Worker):

- POST /api/ask, natural-language product search (Indonesian + English, Vyce intent parsing with a regex fallback)
- POST /api/risk-score, seller risk score with AI explanation
- POST /api/total-cost, honest total with trouble-costs
- POST /api/hold-risk, hold prediction
- POST /api/hold-checklist, hold release checklist
- POST /api/import-cost, duty + VAT/GST per country
- POST /api/phishing-check, phishing verdict + AI review
- POST /api/dispute/simulate, dispute win-chance estimate
- GET /api/evidence?vaultId=, printable proof page (JSON { html })
- POST /api/check-link, link metadata check
- GET /api/deadlines, dispute/return deadlines
- POST /api/paypal/create-order, POST /api/paypal/capture-order, Sandbox checkout
- POST /api/paypal/refund, GET /api/paypal/order, refund and live order status
- GET /api/vault, POST /api/dispute/draft, Proof Vault and simulated dispute draft
- GET /api/marketplace/search, real eBay listings (needs eBay developer keys; dormant until approved)

## Facts and limits

- Built for the PayPal AI Hackathon (deadline 13 Nov 2026). Solo project by Fahriannor (Indonesia).
- Stack: Node.js + Express server, vanilla JS frontend, PayPal Sandbox (OAuth, Orders API v2, Payments API v2), Vyce API (DeepSeek) for AI explanations, deployed as a Cloudflare Worker.
- The demo catalog has 10 products from 3 sellers (TechHub Official, GadgetZone ID, DealHunter88). It does not search real marketplaces; a real eBay adapter is built and waits for eBay developer approval.
- All fees, deadlines, and hold estimates are labelled as estimates, not quotes or guarantees. Scores are a decision aid, not a PayPal guarantee.
- The Worker Proof Vault is memory-only (no durable storage on the free tier). The static demo's vault lives in the browser's localStorage.
- Vyce (DeepSeek) is slow, roughly 13–30 seconds per call; AI explanations have a 30–45 second timeout and fall back to rule-based reasons.
